title: Energy stored in the spring
caption: The force grows from 0 to 40 N as the spring is compressed 5 cm, so the work done is the area of the triangle under the line: ½ × 40 × 0.05 = 1.0 J, not F × x. That energy launches the 20 g ball at √(2 × 1.0/0.02) = 10 m s⁻¹.
alt: Graph of force against compression for a spring of stiffness 800 newtons per metre: a straight line to 40 newtons at 5 centimetres, with the triangle under it shaded and labelled 1.0 joule.
description: The horizontal axis is compression x in m; the vertical axis is force F in N.
F = 800x reaches 40 N at x = 0.05 m.
The shaded triangle has area ½Fx = ½ × 40 × 0.05 = 1.0 J: the stored elastic energy.
All of it becomes kinetic energy: ½ × 0.02 × v² = 1.0 J, so v = 10 m s⁻¹.
